translation_direction: ja → vi; direct from the specifically identified complete Japanese electronic witness
ai_disclosure: Direct AI-produced Vietnamese prose by Claude Opus 5.5. The drafting system conducted the final full assessment; a separate-context assessment by the same model family read every pair and supplied findings first. No human translator, editor, reviewer, independent model consensus or actual reader feedback is recorded.

entry_conditions: Complete named-source and Vietnamese texts, explicit alignment and exact content hashes.
Compare every source and target passage; disclose that this assessor also revised the text and has seen earlier AI assessments.
Source and target edition titles are present and compared explicitly; the title review must match both catalog title strings exactly.
exit_conditions: One complete AI review with a weighted score at least 8.6 using the five unchanged weights and half-point category scores; no separate numerical dimension floors.
All canonical passages reviewed; no unresolved major or critical finding; source and target hashes match the final text.
Publication and rights status are recorded separately in the edition catalog; an AI score does not supply a license.
The selected review includes source_title, target_title and a substantive title rationale; changed titles require a fresh matching review.
review_process.human_feedback: Optional after publication or while a work remains a draft; no prior human publication review is required by v2.

decisions.decision: Concise, slightly archaic Vietnamese with added punctuation for the unpunctuated classical text; Bashō’s parallelism and restraint kept.
The 1911 base text is followed, including its variants, with the one standard emendation recorded.

revision_history.scope: Complete initial direct translation, separate-context full source/target assessment and concrete revisions before the selected final review.

changes.explanation: 夏草や兵どもが夢の跡 de-padded: the cut restored and 跡 rendered as traces (dấu mộng).
蘆角一声の心をやはらげ reparsed: haikai softens hearts used only to rustic reed-pipe tunes; 爰に至れり no longer ‘the peak’.
Padding removed from haiku 6, 3, 36, 46, 50, 88 and 138; the cut marker unified as a dash; 入れたり made transitive (106); あらたふと as praise of the object (12).
木綿しめ, 宝冠, 一睡, そこそこと教ふ, 憐愍, わりなし, みさぶらひみかさ and several calques corrected; En no Gyōja named (21).

selection_limit: Chosen for a complete, directly sourced and openly reusable Vietnamese edition. Existing Vietnamese translations, their quality and reader demand have not been comprehensively assessed; no absence or superiority claim is made.

glossary.draft_rendering: three short Vietnamese lines; the cut (や/かな/けり) as a dash or pause; the poet’s name on a fourth line
glossary.rationale: Keeps image order and the cut without padding; Bashō’s own poems carry no name line.

glossary.draft_rendering: Hán-Việt (Đỗ Phủ, Lý Bạch, Tây Thi, Động Đình, Tây Hồ, Đọa Lệ)
glossary.rationale: Bashō quotes Chinese classics as Vietnamese readers know them.

glossary.draft_rendering: Hepburn romaji; puns carried inside the sentence (Kurokami ‘Tóc Đen’, Urami, Gassan ‘Núi Trăng’)
glossary.rationale: The edition has no notes, so the place-name wordplay is folded into the text.

witness_decision: Selected the Japanese Wikisource page «おくのほそ道» (revision 235001), marked 100% text quality, whose stated base is 三宅邦吉『新釈奥の細道』(籾山書店, 1911; NDL 888916). Only Bashō’s base text is used; the transcription’s 78 variant-reading notes and inline readings are excluded. First printed 1702 (井筒屋本); not collated with the 1702 print or the Soryū manuscript.

unresolved_questions.explanation: The base text’s 露 (for the usual 鶴) is followed, which makes Sora’s Matsushima haiku unusual.

title_review.rationale: Lối lên miền Oku is the established Vietnamese title (Vĩnh Sính’s translation); lên fits a journey north, and the body names the Oku no hosomichi itself.

passage_assessment_notes.assessment: Opening allusion to Li Bai’s ‘passing guests of a hundred generations’.
Best-known haiku kept lean, with their cuts.
